NFL DFS Tight End Rankings: Week 11 (DraftKings)

DraftKings main slate · Sunday, November 22 · 10 games · By Chris Spags · · Numbers as of November 22, 11:59 AM ET

Trey McBride is the top-projected tight end on the Week 11 DraftKings main slate at 14.1 DraftKings points for $6,600, at Kansas City. Colston Loveland (13.2, $5,100) and Isaiah Likely (12.3, $5,600) are next.

Mark Andrews returns the most per dollar among tight ends projected for at least 7 points: 2.68 projected points per $1,000 at $3,500.

Every projection is a SPAGS model estimate from the November 22, 11:59 AM ET run of the Splash Play NFL model. This page updates each time the main-slate numbers are published.

Tight ends to know in Week 11

Trey McBride, ARI at KC ($6,600)

Trey McBride carries the highest SPAGS model projection at the position, 14.1 DraftKings points at $6,600. That is 0.9 points clear of Colston Loveland. The model gives him 11.9 targets on 34.8 routes. The salary works out to 2.14 projected points per $1,000, 11th of 13 at the position. Across 10,000 simulations McBride averaged 14.1 points with a simulated floor of 2.5 and a ceiling of 37.4, and he holds 4% of the simulated winning-lineup credit. Arizona is a 15.5-point underdog on the road against Kansas City, with an implied team total of 12.5 in a game totaled at 40.5.

Colston Loveland, CHI vs NO ($5,100)

Colston Loveland projects 2nd at the position with 13.2 DraftKings points at $5,100. The model gives him 5.6 targets on 21.6 routes. The salary works out to 2.58 projected points per $1,000, 3rd of 13 at the position. Across 10,000 simulations Loveland averaged 13.1 points with a simulated floor of 2.3 and a ceiling of 35.3, and he holds 15% of the simulated winning-lineup credit. Chicago is an 11.5-point favorite at home against New Orleans, with an implied team total of 29.5 in a game totaled at 47.5.

Value: Mark Andrews, BAL at CAR ($3,500)

Mark Andrews projects for 9.4 DraftKings points at $3,500, which works out to 2.68 points per $1,000 of salary. That is the best rate of any player priced in the cheaper half of the 13 tight ends the model projects for 7 or more points. The model gives him 4.8 targets on 20.1 routes. Across 10,000 simulations Andrews averaged 9.5 points with a simulated floor of 0.0 and a ceiling of 32.2, and he holds 11% of the simulated winning-lineup credit. Baltimore is a 2.5-point underdog on the road against Carolina, with an implied team total of 21 in a game totaled at 44.5.
